lau-tha-phan-thiet.name: Phan Thiet Lau Tha Hot Pot
province: Lam Dong (Phan Thiet, former Binh Thuan Province)
lau-tha-phan-thiet.serving_basis: Four servings, with ca mai, vermicelli and greens arranged separately around a pot of hot broth.
lau-tha-phan-thiet.description: A Phan Thiet hot pot centered on fresh ca mai and a colorful spread of accompaniments. This Bep Viet home version serves it with a light shrimp, tomato and pineapple broth.
lau-tha-phan-thiet.finished_dish: A fragrant shrimp broth with gentle acidity from tomato and pineapple; ca mai, pork, egg and greens are arranged separately for cooking at the table.
lau-tha-phan-thiet.excerpt: A fragrant shrimp broth with gentle acidity from tomato and pineapple; ca mai, pork, egg and greens are arranged separately for cooking at the table.
lau-tha-phan-thiet.serving: Arrange vermicelli, greens, cucumber, pork, egg and ca mai on separate plates. Once the broth boils, cook the fish until opaque, then eat with noodles and greens; add a little sweet-and-sour sauce and roasted peanuts.
tips: Choose very fresh ca mai, clean it thoroughly and keep it chilled; use a separate board and knife for raw fish.
Bring the broth to a steady boil before serving so the fish can cook through when dipped.
Add the dipping sauce gradually so it does not overpower the fish and greens.
lau-tha-phan-thiet.tip: Choose very fresh ca mai, clean it thoroughly and keep it chilled; use a separate board and knife for raw fish.

lau-tha-phan-thiet.image_alt: Phan Thiet lau tha spread with fresh ca mai, vermicelli, pork, egg, vegetables and a bowl of shrimp, tomato and pineapple broth.

ingredients.name: Cleaned ca mai fish
ingredients.notes: Ask the fishmonger to clean it and remove pin bones if needed.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Boil until cooked, cool and slice into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Shredded banana blossom
ingredients.notes: Soak in water with a little lime to slow browning.

ingredients.name: Fresh lettuce and herbs
ingredients.notes: Use lettuce, mint and seasonal herbs.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: Make a thin omelet and slice it.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the ca mai, drain and keep chilled. Briefly season it with some garlic, chili, fish sauce and lime juice; do not leave it at room temperature.
Rinse the shrimp and peel them, reserving the shells for broth. Boil the pork belly until cooked, cool and slice into thin strips.
Make a thin omelet and slice it. Prepare the vermicelli, greens, bean sprouts, cucumber and banana blossom; drain well.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute the shallot and garlic. Add the shrimp shells and stir until fragrant, pour in the water and simmer for 15 minutes; strain out the shells.
Bring the strained broth to a boil. Add tomato, pineapple and peeled shrimp and cook through. Season lightly with fish sauce, sugar and salt.
Pour the boiling broth into a hot-pot vessel. Arrange the ca mai, pork, egg, vermicelli and vegetables separately on a platter.
At the table, dip the fish into the boiling broth until opaque and cooked through. Serve with vermicelli and greens, sweet-and-sour sauce and roasted peanuts.

lau-tha-phan-thiet.time_note: Keep ca mai chilled after cleaning and cook it in the boiling broth before eating.

dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.name: Ca Mau Water-Sprite Shoots Stir-Fried with Tiny Shrimp
aliases: U Minh water-sprite shoots with tiny shrimp
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.serving_basis: One family-style dish for four, served with rice.
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.description: Young, lightly curled water-sprite shoots are quickly stir-fried with tiny shrimp, garlic and seasoning. Tuoi Tre identifies this as a common preparation in the U Minh area; Bep Viet standardizes the amounts for a family meal.
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.finished_dish: Fresh green, lightly crisp shoots coated with sweet shrimp, fragrant garlic and a touch of pepper.
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.excerpt: Fresh green, lightly crisp shoots coated with sweet shrimp, fragrant garlic and a touch of pepper.
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice. A small bowl of gently sweet, sour and spicy fish sauce is an optional accompaniment.
tips: Choose fresh young shoots and remove old leaves and fibrous stems.
Add the shoots as soon as the shrimp turn golden and stir-fry briefly to retain their texture.
If the shoots are very mucilaginous, blanch them quickly and drain thoroughly before stir-frying.
dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.tip: Choose fresh young shoots and remove old leaves and fibrous stems.
search_terms: U Minh water-sprite shoots with tiny shrimp
rau choai from the Mekong Delta
Ca Mau shrimp and greens stir-fry

ingredients.name: Young water-sprite shoots
ingredients.notes: Discard old leaves and keep the tender tips and stems.

preparation_steps.instruction: Pick through the shoots, removing old leaves and fibrous stems. Cut into bite-size lengths, rinse and drain well.
Rinse the shrimp and remove the hard heads if desired. Marinate for 5 minutes with half of the shallot, garlic, fish sauce and pepper.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil in a wok and saute the remaining shallot and garlic until fragrant.
Add the shrimp and stir-fry until just cooked and lightly golden.
Add the shoots and optional seasoning powder. Stir-fry quickly over high heat until just tender but still lightly crisp; serve hot.

dot-choai-xao-tep-ca-mau.time_note: Prepare the greens and shrimp before heating the wok; quick stir-frying helps retain the young shoots' texture.

banh-khao-cao-bang.name: Cao Bang Banh Khao (Pressed Glutinous Rice Cakes)
banh-khao-cao-bang.serving_basis: About 12 small cakes, two or three pieces per person.
banh-khao-cao-bang.description: banh khao is a Lunar New Year cake associated with the Tay and Nung communities of Cao Bang, made from finely milled toasted glutinous rice with a filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat. This Bep Viet home adaptation rests the pressed cakes in a clean lined mold.
banh-khao-cao-bang.finished_dish: Small ivory-colored cakes with fragrant, airy toasted-rice flour and a lightly sweet filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat.
banh-khao-cao-bang.excerpt: Small ivory-colored cakes with fragrant, airy toasted-rice flour and a lightly sweet filling of peanuts, sesame and pork fat.
banh-khao-cao-bang.serving: Let the cakes set in the mold, then release and cut into small pieces. Serve with hot tea and store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place.
tips: Toast the glutinous rice over low heat, stirring continuously so it turns aromatic without darkening.
Mill the rice very finely and sift it for a smooth, compact cake.
Rest the cakes in a clean mold lined with food-safe paper; never place the flour directly on the floor.
banh-khao-cao-bang.tip: Toast the glutinous rice over low heat, stirring continuously so it turns aromatic without darkening.
search_terms: Tay and Nung banh khao from Cao Bang
banh khao with peanut and sesame filling
Cao Bang Lunar New Year cake
banh-khao-cao-bang.image_alt: Cao Bang banh khao pressed into ivory square cakes, with one cut piece showing a peanut, sesame and pork-fat filling.

ingredients.name: New glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Choose plump, dry grains with no foreign matter.

ingredients.name: Powdered sugar
ingredients.notes: Finely ground rock sugar or confectioners' sugar.

ingredients.name: Pork fat
ingredients.notes: Boil until cooked and dice finely.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add a little at a time to help the flour hold together.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the glutinous rice quickly and let it dry completely. Dice the pork fat, blanch it until cooked and drain.
Toast the peanuts and sesame separately until fragrant. Rub off the peanut skins and coarsely crush the peanuts.
Toss the pork fat with sugar and let it cool. Prepare a clean cake mold lined with food-safe paper.

cooking_steps.instruction: Toast the glutinous rice in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring until pale golden and fragrant. Cool completely, grind very finely and sift.
Mix the rice flour with powdered sugar and salt. Sprinkle in water gradually and rub the mixture between your fingers; stop when it holds together when squeezed but crumbles easily when dropped.
Combine the peanuts, sesame and pork fat for the filling. Press a layer of flour into the mold, add filling in the center, cover with flour and press evenly.
Rest the cake in the mold for 20 minutes, then release carefully and cut into pieces.

banh-khao-cao-bang.time_note: Cool the toasted rice fully before grinding. The amount of water depends on how dry the flour is, so add it gradually.

com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.name: Ninh Binh Crispy Rice with Goat Sauce
aliases: Ninh Binh crispy rice with goat meat sauce
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.serving_basis: Four servings, each with a crisp rice cake and hot goat sauce.
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.description: Ninh Binh crispy rice has a golden, crunchy crust formed in a thick-bottomed pot; it may be served with pork floss or goat sauce. This Bep Viet version pairs it with a family-style tomato and mushroom goat sauce.
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.finished_dish: A golden, airy rice cake topped with lightly thickened goat sauce, tomato and mushrooms; the meat is tender and fragrant with ginger and lemongrass.
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.excerpt: A golden, airy rice cake topped with lightly thickened goat sauce, tomato and mushrooms; the meat is tender and fragrant with ginger and lemongrass.
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.serving: Spoon only enough hot goat sauce over the crispy rice just before eating to keep the exposed surface crisp. Serve hot with herbs or pickled vegetables.
tips: Use a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed pot and keep the rice layer thin so the crust browns evenly.
Dry the rice crust before frying; this helps it puff and reduces oil splatter.
Add the sauce just before serving to keep the rice crisp.
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.tip: Use a cast-iron or heavy-bottomed pot and keep the rice layer thin so the crust browns evenly.
search_terms: Ninh Binh crispy rice with goat sauce
com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.image_alt: Golden Ninh Binh crispy rice topped with goat meat sauce, tomato and mushrooms on a white plate.

ingredients.name: Long-grain rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and pick out any debris.

ingredients.name: Frying oil
ingredients.notes: Enough for deep-frying; use a deep pot.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the rice and cook it with enough water to make tender, slightly sticky rice.
Drain and slice the goat meat. Prepare the tomato, mushrooms, lemongrass, ginger, garlic and shallot.
When the rice is cooked, scoop out the top portion, leaving a thin layer at the bottom of the pot. Gently press it into an even layer, cool, then air-dry or dehydrate until the surface is dry.

cooking_steps.instruction: Keep the heavy-bottomed pot over low heat, rotating it often until the bottom rice layer is evenly golden and releases from the pot. Dry it further if any part remains moist.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot. Fry the dried rice cake until the grains puff and turn crisp and golden; drain.
Marinate the goat meat with fish sauce, pepper and some ginger and lemongrass for 10 minutes. Saute shallot, garlic and remaining aromatics, then add the meat and brown it.
Add tomato, mushrooms and enough water. Simmer until the goat is tender and the sauce lightly thickens. Adjust seasoning and add scallion if desired.
Place the crispy rice on a plate and spoon the hot goat sauce over it just before serving.

com-chay-sot-de-ninh-binh.time_note: Air-drying time varies with rice-cake thickness and humidity; the crust should feel dry before frying.

pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.name: Ngu Xa Pho Rolls from Ha Noi
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.serving_basis: About 16 rolls, suitable for four light servings or two to three main-meal servings.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.description: Wide pho sheets wrap stir-fried beef and fresh herbs, served with sweet-and-sour fish sauce. This well-known Ngu Xa, Ha Noi dish is adapted by Bep Viet with home-friendly amounts and a compact filling so the rolls stay neat.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.finished_dish: Soft white pho sheets filled with fragrant garlic beef, lettuce and herbs, served with balanced sweet-and-sour dipping sauce.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.excerpt: Soft white pho sheets filled with fragrant garlic beef, lettuce and herbs, served with balanced sweet-and-sour dipping sauce.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.serving: Arrange the rolls on a platter with a bowl of sweet-and-sour fish sauce with garlic and chili. Serve while the beef is aromatic and the pho sheets are soft.
tips: Choose wide pho sheets that are soft but not overly wet so the rolls hold their shape.
Let the beef cool slightly before rolling to keep the pho sheets from tearing.
Do not overfill; place the greens in the middle and roll snugly.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.tip: Choose wide pho sheets that are soft but not overly wet so the rolls hold their shape.
pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.image_alt: Ngu Xa pho rolls with soft white rice sheets, stir-fried beef, lettuce and herbs, served with sweet-and-sour fish sauce.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse and drain the greens and cucumber. Cut the cucumber into long batons.
Slice the beef thinly across the grain and marinate with some fish sauce, pepper and garlic for 10 minutes.
If needed, cut long pho sheets into rectangles for rolling; keep them covered with a clean cloth so they do not dry out.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute some of the garlic until fragrant. Stir-fry the beef quickly over high heat until just cooked, then let it cool slightly.
Lay a pho sheet on a clean surface. Place lettuce, herbs, cucumber and beef near one edge; fold in the sides and roll snugly.
Stir the fish sauce with water, sugar and lime juice until the sugar dissolves; add garlic and chili.
Arrange the rolls on a plate and serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

pho-cuon-ngu-xa-ha-noi.time_note: Let the beef cool slightly before rolling; very hot or wet filling can tear the soft pho sheets.
